name: Tabitha
overview: Tabitha was a female disciple who lived in the city of Joppa. The Scriptures identify her specifically by this unique attribute, highlighting her role within the early Christian community. Beyond this, no additional personal details or tribal affiliations are recorded.
namesAndTitles: Tabitha is also known by the name Dorcas, which means 'gazelle.' Both names are proper names mentioned in Acts 9:36, with Dorcas carrying the meaning that reflects gracefulness or beauty, though neither name was given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Tabitha beyond her identification as a disciple in Joppa. There are no listed relatives or connections mentioned in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Tabitha's significance in the biblical narrative rests on her identity as a devoted female disciple in the early church, representing the faithful followers of Christ in Joppa. Her mention in Acts 9:36 underscores the presence and importance of women in the ministry and life of the early Christian community, serving as an example of discipleship.
